rationale: Provisional recommendation: NO as of 2026-10-14. The official original is 85 FR 34079, PDF pages 1-5 (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2020-06-02/pdf/2020-12030.pdf, SHA-256 c1f52245dae8c3c40affe17527d3135490e652436851606ad20bb8e5d307009b); all pages were inspected visually, including signature/closing page. The held official EO EO:14029 copy (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2021-05-19/pdf/2021-10691.pdf, SHA-256 eb3d5e1b1d96e89e74cac80c628b3cb98b0b92c67cc0624794cb1995e3fcb909, 86 FR 27025, PDF pages 1-2) expressly revokes this target in section 1(a) and the instrument date is 2021-05-14; its specific effective-date clause is not separately explicit, so the legal-effective date remains unconfirmed. For EO 13836/13837/13839, a D.D.C. injunction dated 2018-08-25 barred enforcement of specified sections; the D.C. Circuit vacated that judgment and the 2019-10-11 Presidential Memorandum (84 FR 56095, GovInfo https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2019-10-21/pdf/2019-23021.pdf) says the mandate issued and clarifies treatment of CBAs executed during the injunction. This is a scoped temporary enforcement interruption, not a whole-order revocation. EO 14148 (2025-01-20; GovInfo PDF https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-28/pdf/2025-02006.pdf, SHA-256 d658f5158a27f6d4a220ce2ec854bdbd596ecc841fb16884954a2e2ee39ab072) expressly revokes EO 14003 and EO 14029 but does not name or reenact the four target orders. I do not infer revival from revocation of a later rescinding order; the 14148 language and an initial later-source scan support retaining NO, subject to bounded search and legal review. This remains a producer draft: no independent status review, no owner adoption, no complete clause first-ending proof, and residual savings/implementation effects remain open.
